newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent stages late recovery to close higher.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent stages late recovery to close higher.

text.p: IPE Brent closed higher on Tuesday after supply concerns, technicals and expectations of moderately supportive American Petroleum Institute (API) U.S. oil stock data shook it out of its earlier lethargy, traders said.
IPE June Brent settled 34 cents lower at $18.60 a barrel on Tuesday having spent most the day hugging Monday's close.
The contract reversed its lacklustre performance mid-afternoon after U.S. product futures registered strong gains at the NYMEX open.
May Heating oil was trading 2.37 cents higher at 58.90 cents a gallon at 1941 while May gasoline was a 0.96 cent higher at 63.30 cents at 1941 GMT.
Rumours that a U.S. refinery was experiencing problems also helped to kickstart the gains, but this story was soon quashed by NYMEX traders who said a player long in gasoline had initiated it.
Traders said the market was also keenly awaiting American Petroleum Institute (API) data due to be released late on Tuesday.
According to a Reuter survey, analysts expect crude stocks to be down 1.0 million barrels, distillate stocks to be off 1.0 million barrels and gasoline stocks to have fallen 500,000 barrels.
On a technical note, traders said the fact the June IPE contract had managed to push above $18.50 and stay there was also a good sign.
"I didn't think we would get much above $18.50 but we have and closed above it which is quite a positive sign," said one trader.
May gas oil closed $3.0 higher at $169.00 a tonne. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
